extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors submitting manuscripts to The New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM)
extracted.subtask_description: Author instructions and statistical reporting guidelines for preparing and submitting original research, clinical trials, and observational studies to NEJM, including required materials, analytic and reporting standards, and journal style elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal scope and novelty requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: NEJM is interested in publishing original research that is destined to change clinical practice and teaches something new about the biology of disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider whether their work has potential to change clinical practice or brings new biological insight before submitting; presubmission inquiries are available to check suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of presubmission inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors unsure of suitability may send a Presubmission Inquiry; NEJM editors endeavor to respond by email within one week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presubmission inquiries can save time and effort. Invited/commissioned article ideas may also be sent as presubmission inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid review eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for accelerated Rapid Review are considered especially when results: (1) deal with urgent public health concerns, (2) have potential to dramatically change clinical practice or affect mortality, or (3) are timed to imminent meeting presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval for Rapid Review does not guarantee acceptance or expedited publication. NEJM aims to reply to Rapid Review requests within three business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: sample size and power reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Methods section of all manuscripts should contain a brief description of sample size and power considerations for the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the rationale and calculations underlying sample size choices and power for primary and key secondary analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: description of primary and secondary analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Methods section should include a brief description of the methods for primary and secondary analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state analytic approaches for each prespecified outcome and how inferential procedures will be conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Methods section should include a description of how missing data have been handled; unless missingness is rare, a complete-case analysis is generally not acceptable as the primary analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When data are missing at random, consider multiple imputation or inverse-probability weighting; when missingness may be informative, model-based methods may be more appropriate. See NEJM guidance (Ware et al. 2012) for clinical trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompany significance tests with confidence intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance tests should be accompanied by confidence intervals for estimated effect sizes, measures of association, or other parameters of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidence intervals should be adjusted to match any adjustment made to significance levels in the corresponding test (e.g., adjustments for multiplicity).

rubrics_metrics.name: P-value conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless one-sided tests are required by study design (such as in noninferiority trials), all reported P values should be two-sided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report P values >0.01 to two decimal places, P values between 0.01 and 0.001 to three decimal places; report P<0.001 for P values smaller than 0.001. Exceptions include P values from stopping-rule tests or genome-wide association studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Results should be presented with no more precision than is of scientific value and is meaningful given the available sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures of association (e.g., odds ratios) should ordinarily be reported to two significant digits. Results derived from models should be limited to an appropriate number of significant digits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trials: submission of protocols and SAPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Original and final protocols and statistical analysis plans (SAPs) should be submitted along with the manuscript, plus a table of amendments indicating date and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocols may be redacted of proprietary information but must include information on patient flow and outcomes. Editors may request more information on redacted protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trials: adherence to prespecified analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The analyses of the primary outcome in manuscripts reporting clinical trials should match the analyses prespecified in the original protocol, except in unusual circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses that do not conform to the protocol should be justified in the Methods section. Editors may request additional analyses not specified in the protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of overall type I error in confirmatory comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: When comparing outcomes in two or more groups in confirmatory analyses, investigators should use the testing procedures specified in the protocol and SAP to control overall type I error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Bonferroni adjustments or prespecified hierarchical procedures. P values adjusted for multiplicity should be reported when appropriate and labeled as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchical testing reporting rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In hierarchical testing procedures, P values should be reported only until the last comparison for which the P value was statistically significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P values for the first nonsignificant comparison and for all comparisons thereafter should not be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prespecified exploratory analyses and FDR control
rubrics_metrics.description: For prespecified exploratory analyses, investigators should use methods for controlling false discovery rate described in the SAP (for example, Benjamini–Hochberg procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the SAP documents the chosen FDR method and how it will be applied to exploratory endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting when no multiplicity adjustment prespecified
rubrics_metrics.description: When no method to adjust for multiplicity or control false discovery rate was specified in the protocol or SAP, reports of all secondary and exploratory endpoints should be limited to point estimates with 95% confidence intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Methods section should note that the widths of the intervals have not been adjusted for multiplicity and that inferences may not be reproducible. No P values should be reported for these analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prespecified subgroup analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: When the SAP prespecifies an analysis of certain subgroups, that analysis should conform to the method described in the SAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the prespecified method in the SAP and follow it exactly for subgroup inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post hoc subgroup analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: If the study team believes a post hoc analysis of subgroups is important, the rationale for conducting that analysis should be stated and such analyses should be clearly labeled as post hoc in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly distinguish post hoc findings from prespecified subgroup analyses to avoid overstating evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forest plots and subgroup interaction p-values
rubrics_metrics.description: Forest plots are often used to present results from analyses of the consistency of a treatment effect across subgroups and are recommended for important subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subgroups are small, formal inferences about homogeneity may not be feasible. A list of P values for treatment-by-subgroup interactions is subject to multiplicity problems and has limited value; in most cases, no P values for interaction should be provided in forest plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety outcomes multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: If significance tests of safety outcomes (when not primary outcomes) are reported along with treatment-specific estimates, no adjustment for multiplicity is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because safety endpoints may signal problems within organ classes, type I error rates larger than 0.05 are acceptable. Editors may request P values for comparisons of adverse-event frequencies among treatment groups regardless of prespecification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer absolute counts before relative measures
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, editors prefer that absolute event counts or rates be reported before relative risks or hazard ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing both actual event frequency and relative frequency helps interpretation. Avoid odds ratios where they may overestimate relative risks and be misinterpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT flow diagram and checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should provide a CONSORT-format flow diagram and are encouraged to submit the CONSORT checklist and flow diagram with clinical-trial manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not all information may be published, provide CONSORT materials in the manuscript or supplementary appendix at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational studies: address selection and confounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods sections of observational studies should describe how sample selection, measured and unmeasured confounding, and adequacy of methods used to control confounding were managed in design and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about strategies used (design features, measured confounder adjustment, instrumental variables, propensity scores, etc.) and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational studies: prespecified SAPs and deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If an observational study included a prespecified SAP, a signed and dated version should be included with the manuscript submission; the journal encourages depositing SAPs for observational studies in online repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositing SAPs increases transparency and credibility of observational analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational studies: multiple testing
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, observational studies should use prespecified accepted methods for controlling family-wise error rate or false discovery rate when multiple tests are conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In manuscripts reporting observational studies without a prespecified method, summary statistics should be limited to point estimates and 95% confidence intervals; no P values should be reported for these analyses, and Methods should note the lack of multiplicity adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: When no prespecified analysis plan exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If no prespecified analysis plan exists, the Methods section should provide an outline for the planned method of analysis including eligibility criteria and sampling method (with a diagram as appropriate), description of the association or causal effect to be estimated and rationale, and the prespecified method of analysis to draw inference about treatment or exposure effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail that readers can assess validity of design and analysis decisions made after data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display of confounders and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies reporting effect of a treatment or exposure should show the distribution of potential confounders and other variables, stratified by exposure or intervention group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyses depend on confounders being balanced by exposure group, differences between groups should be summarized with point estimates and 95% confidence intervals when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex models and diagnostics in supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex models and their diagnostics can often be best described in a supplementary appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide model-building details, diagnostics, and sensitivity analyses in the appendix rather than crowding the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to unmeasured confounding and replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to conduct analyses that quantify potential sensitivity to bias from unmeasured confounding; absent that, authors must provide a discussion of potential biases induced by unmeasured confounders and are encouraged to retest findings in similar but independent studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include formal sensitivity analyses when feasible or thorough discussion of plausible unmeasured-confounding effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units of measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should express all measurements in conventional units, with Système International (SI) units given in parentheses throughout the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures and tables should use conventional units, with conversion factors given in legends or footnotes. Manuscripts containing only SI units will not be returned for that reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for units of measurement, abbreviations are strongly discouraged; the first time an abbreviation appears it should be preceded by the words for which it stands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize use of abbreviations to improve readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug-naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic names should be used; when proprietary brands are used in research, include the brand name and the name of the manufacturer in parentheses after the first mention of the generic name in the Methods section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies what exact product was used while prioritizing generic nomenclature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letters are not required, but the NEJM online submission system contains a text field where important information not in metadata (such as meeting presentation date or a major conflict of interest not in the manuscript) can be communicated with initial submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cover-letter field to highlight contextual information that editors should know at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript file format and compilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compile all text, references, figure legends, and tables into a single double-spaced digital file (preferably an MS Word document). NEJM will also accept .txt or .rtf files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the single file contains main text and that figures may be uploaded separately; low-resolution images ok for peer review but high-resolution may be requested later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page content
rubrics_metrics.description: Title page must include manuscript title; each author's name, highest degree, and affiliation/institution; and contact information for one corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete and accurate contact and affiliation details to facilitate editorial communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract structure and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an abstract of not more than 250 words with four labeled paragraphs: Background, Methods, Results, Conclusions. Include trial registration number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the four-paragraph labeled format exactly and keep within the word limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying data requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At appropriate places, provide statements that the research protocol was approved by relevant IRBs or ethics committees and that all human participants gave written informed consent; identify those who analyzed the data; provide trial registration numbers and microarray accession numbers where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include registry name and number for clinical trials and accession numbers/repository names for molecular data.

rubrics_metrics.name: References formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: References must be double-spaced and numbered consecutively as cited. List all authors when there are six or fewer; when seven or more, list first three followed by et al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References first cited in a table or figure legend should be numbered so they are in sequence with text citations. Numbered references to personal communications, unpublished data, or manuscripts 'in preparation' or 'submitted' are unacceptable; such material can be incorporated into text if essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: placement, spacing, and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables should be included at the end of the manuscript text file, double-spaced (including footnotes), and provide a title for each table. For Original Articles there is normally a limit of five figures and tables (total) per manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive tables or supplementary materials will be published as supplemental materials with the digital version of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and technical quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can insert figures into text files (preferred) or upload figure files separately. Low-resolution images may be submitted for peer review, but high-resolution versions complying with Technical Guidelines may be requested later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each figure should include a title and a legend on the same page as the figure. Follow journal's technical guidelines when preparing final figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary appendix format
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript's Supplementary Appendix should be paginated, with a table of contents, followed by a list of investigators (if any), text (such as methods), figures, tables, and then references. Appendix citations and reference list should be self-contained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Appendix must be submitted in two formats: PDF and MS Word (or another editable text format). The Appendix will not be edited for style and will be presented online as additional information provided by the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary figures/tables: outcome scales
rubrics_metrics.description: For outcome scales, provide in the figure legend or table footnotes the range, sign, and minimally important difference (if known), with an informative reference citation for the scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label Supplementary Appendix tables as Table S1, Table S2, etc., and accompany each with a title and, if necessary, footnotes.
